step1_figure.circuit_type: NMOS differential amplifier with cascode tail current source and drains tied to VDD
step1_figure.description: Figure 22.2 depicts an NMOS differential pair (M1 and M2) with drains tied directly to the positive supply (VDD = 5 V in the text, 1.8 V in Sky130) and sources tied together to an NMOS cascode tail current sink biased by Vbias3 and Vbias4 from a wide-swing bias circuit (Fig. 20.43).

tail_current_iss.description: Total quiescent tail bias current sunk by the NMOS cascode current source (M6t/M6b)

equation.explanation: Total current sunk by the cascode tail current source under balanced input conditions
equation.assumptions: Both input devices M1 and M2 are active and tail transistors are in saturation

sky130_expected.calculation: With R1 = 6.5 kOhm in the wide-swing reference (SUB_1) and 20/1 aspect ratio for the cascode mirror devices, the nominal tail current scales to ~20 uA - 40 uA. For ISS = 20 uA, branch currents are 10 uA each.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Determined by the Beta-multiplier self-biasing reference current generator.

quiescent_branch_current.description: Quiescent drain current in M1 and M2 when differential input voltage is zero (vI1 = vI2)

equation.explanation: When inputs are equal (vI1 = vI2 = 0.9 V), the tail current splits equally between M1 and M2
equation.assumptions: M1 and M2 are matched and both operate in the saturation region

sky130_expected.calculation: I_D1 = I_D2 = I_SS / 2 = 20 uA / 2 = 10 uA (or 20 uA if ISS = 40 uA).
sky130_expected.reasoning: Symmetry ensures equal splitting when gate voltages are identical.

vi1_max_steering.description: Maximum gate voltage on M1 where M1 steers all tail current ISS, turning off M2

equation.formula: v_I1,MAX = sqrt((2 * L * I_SS) / (KP_n * W)) + v_I2
equation.explanation: Input voltage above vI2 at which the source voltage rises high enough that M2 gate-to-source voltage drops below threshold, steering all current through M1
equation.assumptions: Square-law saturation model without velocity saturation

sky130_expected.reasoning: The differential input range for complete steering is sqrt(2)*V_ov above vI2.

vi1_min_steering.description: Minimum gate voltage on M1 where M1 shuts off and M2 steers all tail current ISS

equation.formula: v_I1,MIN = v_I2 - sqrt((2 * L * I_SS) / (KP_n * W))
equation.explanation: Input voltage below vI2 where M1 turns off completely

sky130_expected.reasoning: Symmetric lower bound of differential input linear steering window.

vcm_max.description: Maximum common-mode input voltage maintaining M1 and M2 in saturation

equation.explanation: Since drains are tied directly to VDD, the input common-mode voltage can exceed VDD by one threshold voltage before M1 and M2 leave saturation and enter triode

sky130_expected.calculation: V_CMMAX = V_DD + V_THN = 1.8 V + 0.42 V = 2.22 V.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Drain is tied to 1.8 V; NMOS enters triode when VDS < VGS - VTHN => VG > VD + VTHN.

vcm_min.description: Minimum common-mode input voltage keeping M1, M2 and cascode tail current source in saturation

equation.explanation: The gates of M1 and M2 must be high enough to support the gate-to-source voltage plus the minimum compliance voltage across the two cascode current source transistors
equation.assumptions: Minimum voltage across the cascode current sink is 2 * V_DS,sat

sky130_expected.reasoning: Limited by the threshold voltage and overdrive of the input pair plus compliance of cascode sink.

small_signal_transconductance.description: Small-signal transconductance gm of input devices M1 and M2 at equilibrium

equation.formula: g_m = sqrt(KP_n * (W / L) * I_SS) = 2 * I_D / V_ov
equation.explanation: Small-signal transconductance determining the differential current response id = gm * vdi / 2
equation.assumptions: M1 and M2 operate in saturation at balanced DC operating point

sky130_expected.reasoning: Calculated directly from Sky130 parameters KP_n = 270 uA/V^2 and W/L = 10.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench measuring tail current, balanced branch currents, input current steering range (vI1_min and vI1_max), common-mode input limits, and transconductance for the NMOS differential amplifier.
